subject: Operational plan for tenant 'no-model-improvement' routing, KMS residency, and prompt/response custody
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha@clearpathhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Tenant-level no-model-improvement option + operational asks

Hi Marissa / David,

Thanks for the product overview this morning — the demo clarified a lot. A couple of items the legal & security teams asked me to confirm before we move to signatures: 

1) We need an operational description of how requests tagged as "no-model-improvement" (tenant-level opt-out) are handled end-to-end. Specifically: routing, storage, and whether prompt/response artifacts are ever persisted outside ephemeral KV for debugging.

2) KMS residency: ClearPath requires onshore (US) CMEK for customer-derived artifacts that are stored for >24 hours. We’d like details on what artifacts might be stored and where keys are used.

3) Prompt/response ownership: the DPA redline proposes "Customer retains ownership of prompts and responses" but legal wants clarity on derivative rights — do you treat responses as customer data (no training rights) and will Redwood assert any rights to derivative improvements?

We attached our current subprocessor list and proposed DPA amendment (see attachments). Can you provide an operational note (1–2 pages) we can pass to our InfoSec, and a target timeline for evidence or attestation?

Thanks,
Samantha
Security Program Manager
ClearPath Health

[Attachment: clearpath_subprocessor_list_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: david_kim <david@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-14T11:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Tenant-level no-model-improvement option + operational asks

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. I’ve sketched an operational note below and attached a short draft you can circulate. High-level summary first, then technical/operational bullets.

Operational summary (TL;DR):
- Tenant-level "no-model-improvement" (NMIP) is enforced at the request router and tagging layer. Any request with the NMIP flag is routed to a dedicated tenant lane where telemetry and payloads are isolated from model improvement pipelines.
- Ephemeral KV: by default responses are kept only in ephemeral KV for the duration of the session (max 24 hours) and are not written to long-term telemetry stores or training buckets.
- Onshore KMS: when a customer requests onshore CMEK, we provision tenant-scoped key wrapping for any persisted artifacts and ensure storage nodes are within the US region (AWS us-west-2/us-east-1 options).
- Prompt/response ownership: Redwood will not assert training rights over NMIP-tagged interactions; responses and prompts are treated as customer data subject to the DPA amendment. Redwood retains the right to aggregate telemetry (token counts, latency metrics) only in anonymized form.

Operational details (short):
- Request ingress: NMIP flag is set via API header x-redwood-no-model-improve or via console config per tenant.
- Routing: router inspects flag, sends traffic to a dedicated serving pool that has model variants with learning disabled and has separate logging sinks.
- KV/storage: ephemeral KV retained up to 24 hours for session continuity. Any telemetry written to durable stores is stripped of user prompt/response payloads unless customer requests otherwise via explicit export APIs.
- KMS/CMEK: when CMEK onshore is requested, we bind tenant storage buckets to the customer’s onshore key (we use AES256-GCM wrapped by the customer key). Access audits are recorded and provided as part of evidence pack.
- Subprocessors: we will exclude analytics/annotation subprocessors from processing NMIP-tagged content; subprocessor gating is enforced in the ingest pipeline. See attached subprocessor gating matrix.

Evidence & timeline:
- Subprocessor attestation and filtered list: 3 business days (we can provide a redacted attestation pack).
- KMS routing diagram + proof-of-residency (cloud region & bucket names with IAM snapshots): 5 business days.
- DPA amendment draft with explicit "no training" clause and prompt/response ownership language: updated draft attached.

Next steps:
1) Confirm you want onshore CMEK for persisted artifacts (yes/no).
2) If yes, can we get your KMS key ARN or let us know if Redwood should provision tenant-scoped keys under an SOC2-limited escrow arrangement?
3) We’ll share an evidence pack by end-of-week once you confirm KMS direction.

I’m looping Kim (legal) and David (privacy/ops) — Kim, adding a few redline items we think make the DPA operationally testable.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: draft-dpa-no-improve-amendment.docx (docx)]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Li <samantha@clearpathhealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Operational plan for tenant 'no-model-improvement' routing, KMS residency, and prompt/response custody

Marissa / team — quick legal clarifications that ClearPath might accept to make the DPA redline unambiguous: 

1) "No training" clause: propose the explicit language: "Redwood shall not use Customer Prompts or Customer Responses for model training, fine-tuning, or parameter updates, now or in the future, for any internal or external model development activities." This covers future model reuse concerns.

2) Definition of "Customer Responses": include model-generated completions, summaries, and any transformed outputs derived from Customer Prompts. Avoid vague language like "derivatives" without context.

3) Audit & proof scope: define what evidence satisfies the clause (subprocessor attestations, KMS key snapshots, object lifecycle policies demonstrating deletion after 24 hours). We should offer a signed statement and sample IAM/S3 object lifecycle screenshots.

4) Emergency debug carveout: to accommodate critical incident response, add a limited, auditable carveout allowing Redwood to persist a copy of specific NMIP-tagged interactions for up to 72 hours with customer approval (explicit ticket + retention metadata). That should be opt-in per incident and fully logged.

I recommend we include the above as redlines in the draft. If ClearPath confirms onshore CMEK and the emergency debug carveout process, we can finalize language and deliver the proof artifacts.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

(Internal note: we should prepare the IAM snapshot pack — David, can your team pull lifecycle configs and the KMS binding test?)

From: Samantha Li <samantha@clearpathhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Operational plan for tenant 'no-model-improvement' routing, KMS residency, and prompt/response custody

Kimberly / Marissa — this all looks good and more prescriptive than our original ask, which helps. A couple quick responses: 

- ClearPath confirms we want onshore CMEK for persisted artifacts. I’ll share the key ARN via our secure portal (will send before EOD tomorrow).
- The "no training" language you proposed is acceptable to Legal; please include it in the next redline.
- The emergency debug carveout is reasonable — we’ll want a one-time approval workflow that includes our SOC/contact and a signed ticket.

Please proceed with the evidence pack (subproc attestations + IAM/Lifecycle screenshots) and the redlined DPA. Our procurement team will expect the DocuSign link once Legal accepts the redline.

Thanks — looking forward to the packs.
Samantha
Security Program Manager
ClearPath Health
